title: A cohomology Tor interval bounds the Tor interval of a bounded complex
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_X))$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $a\leq b$ and $c\leq d$ be integers. Suppose $H^q(K)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$ and, for every $q\in[a,b]$, the module $H^q(K)$ in degree zero has Tor amplitude in $[c,d]$ [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. Then $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a+c,b+d]$. No constructibility assumption on its cohomology is required.

source.place: Complexes, truncation induction with a general common cohomology Tor interval

proof.text: Put $C=\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_X)$, $I=[a+c,b+d]$, and let $Q(L)$ mean Tor amplitude in $I$. The Tor-amplitude well-definedness statement makes $Q$ invariant under isomorphism and closed under extensions in distinguished triangles. For a zero object, use isomorphism invariance to replace it by $0[0]$. For every test module $N$, the relative single-tensor model with $M=0$ and $q=0$ has all terms zero, hence all cohomology zero. Thus every zero object satisfies $Q$. The interval is ordered since $a\leq b$ and $c\leq d$.

source.place: Complexes, truncation induction with a general common cohomology Tor interval

proof.text: For each integer $q$, let $P_q(M)$ mean $a\leq q\leq b$ and Tor amplitude $[c,d]$ for $M[0]$. This property is invariant under isomorphism by Tor-amplitude well-definedness. For relative tensor, the unsigned $s^1_{-q}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts] gives the total-complex shift comparison; the relative single-tensor node supplies its Layer-B model and derived cohomology comparison. If $P_q(M)$ holds, apply that comparison to every test module $N$: its degree-$r$ cohomology is zero when $r-q\notin[c,d]$. Thus $M[0][-q]$ has amplitude $[q+c,q+d]$. Since $a\leq q\leq b$, this interval lies in $I$; vanishing outside the smaller interval implies vanishing outside $I$. This supplies $Q(M[0][-q])$ for every $q,M$ satisfying $P_q(M)$, including negative $q$.

source.place: Complexes, truncation induction with a general common cohomology Tor interval

proof.text: Apply degreewise bounded dévissage to $C,Q,P_q$, $n=b-a+1\in\mathbf N$ and lower bound $a$. Then $a+n-1=b$ and $a\leq q<a+n$ is precisely $q\in[a,b]$. The hypotheses on $K$ supply cohomological vanishing outside that interval and $P_q(H^q(K))$ inside it. The preceding steps supply every other hypothesis of dévissage. Its conclusion $Q(K)$ is exactly the required Tor amplitude $[a+c,b+d]$. No constructibility or geometric finiteness hypothesis was used.

source.place: Complexes, truncation induction with a general common cohomology Tor interval
